Marks-only display list (internal, for vellumwidget)

Source: R/display-list.R
scene_display_list.Rd

Resolves every keyed mark in a scene to device-pixel geometry, a paint and its key, packed as compact columnar tables. vellumwidget ships this to the browser to draw and hit-test big plots (F-5 stage 1).

Usage

scene_display_list(
  scene,
  what = "keyed",
  panels = NULL,
  version = 1L,
  keys = NULL,
  precision = "f32"
)

Arguments

scene

A vl_scene(), or anything with an as_vellum_scene() method.

what

Which marks to list. Only "keyed" for now.

panels

NULL (the default) to list keyed marks wherever they are, or a character vector of panel names to list only those whose innermost named panel (scene_model()$elements$panel) is one of them, the same rule as scene_png(layer = "keyed", panels = ). vellumwidget passes its data panels, which leaves out a legend's keyed swatches.

version

The format version, 1 (the default) or 2 (see the Version 2 section).

keys

NULL (the default), or a character vector of keys for record$key to index, so the list need not repeat them (VR-22). Keys it lacks are listed in keys as usual, after it; NA matches nothing.

precision

How to encode the geometry columns (see Compact coordinates): "f32" (the default) for 32-bit floats; "u16" or "u24" to quantise each column to 16 or 24 bits within its range; or a positive number, the largest rounding error allowed in device px, to use the fewest of 8, 16 or 24 bits that keeps each column within it (f32 when none does). 0.005, half the 0.01 px grid scene_svg() writes coordinates on, takes 16 bits for a column spanning up to 655 px.

Value

The display list, as described in the Format section.

Details

This is a private vellum to vellumwidget payload, not a public format. Its fields and encodings may change in any release, in step with vellumwidget. Do not build on it.

Format

A list with format = "vellum-display-list", version (1 or 2), the page width and height in device px, the record count n, and:

  • record: one row per keyed primitive, in paint order. kind (0 point, 1 rect, 2 path), paint (0-based row of paints), key (0-based index into keys), flags (bitfield, see below), clip (1-based row of clips, 0 = unclipped) and panel (1-based into panels: the innermost named panel the mark is drawn in, as in scene_model()$elements$panel; 0 = none). The i-th record of a kind is the i-th row of that kind's table.

  • point: cx, cy, r (device px) and shape (0 circle, else the points_grob() marker code: 1 square, 2 triangle, 3 diamond, 4 plus, 5 cross, 6 triangle down, 7 star).

  • rect: axis-aligned rectangles, top-left x, y and size w, h.

  • path: polygons and polylines. xy holds interleaved vertices, run_offset the start of each run in vertices (one more entry than runs), path_offset the start of each path in runs (one more than paths), closed (1 = closed rings, 0 = open polylines) and evenodd (fill rule). Curves are flattened.

  • paints: a data-frame-like list with fill and stroke ("#rrggbbaa" or NA for none), stroke_width (device px), dash (comma-separated device px, or NA for solid), linecap and linejoin.

  • clips: rectangles x0, y0, x1, y1 (device px).

  • keys: the distinct keys in first-use order, as a character vector, or as an integer column (see below) when every key is a plain non-negative integer. With the keys argument, only the keys it lacks (see below).

  • keys_given: only with the keys argument, its length. record$key then indexes c(<the keys argument>, keys): a key found in the argument is its first position there, and the rest follow in first-use order. A client that already has the keys (vellumwidget's element table) ships them once.

  • panels: the names of the panels marks are drawn in.

Every numeric column except those in paints and clips is a list list(type, n, ...). type is "f32", "u8", "u16" or "u32" (or "u24", see below), and n is the length. The values come as exactly one of data (base64, little-endian, typed), const (every value equal), seq = c(start, step) (an arithmetic sequence) or rle = list(values, lengths) (runs of equal values, used when there are few).

Compact coordinates

With precision other than "f32" (VR-18), the geometry columns (point cx, cy, r; rect x, y, w, h; path xy) are quantised within their own range: such a column is list(type, n, lo, step, data) with type "u8", "u16" or "u24" (three bytes per value) and value i lo + u[i] * step, where u are the little-endian unsigned integers in data, lo is the column's minimum and step its range over 2^bits - 1. The rounding error is at most step / 2. A column that is empty, collapses to const or rle or holds a non-finite value stays f32, as do the clip_paths coordinates. Points come in paint order, not in space, so their coordinates are not delta-coded: neighbouring records are as far apart as any two.

Version 2

version = 2 lists three more cases exactly, which version 1 flags, and adds the tables they need. A reader that knows only version 1 must not be handed a version-2 list: their records are no longer flagged.

  • Gradient fills: linear and radial gradients with pad extension. paints$fill_gradient is the 1-based row of gradients (0 = none; then fill is NA). gradients has type ("linear" or "radial"), the geometry in the shape's local px (linear: x1, y1 to x2, y2; radial: the focal circle x1, y1, r1 at offset 0 to the outer circle x2, y2, r2 at offset 1), the transform placing it in device px as a, b, c, d, e, f (the SVG / canvas matrix(a, b, c, d, e, f)), and its stops: gradient i's are rows stop_offset[i] + 1 to stop_offset[i + 1] of stop_pos (0 to 1) and stop_color ("#rrggbbaa").

  • Path clips: a clip by a path or a rotated rectangle. clips gains path_start and path_n: a clip's paths are shapes path_start + 1 to path_start + path_n of clip_paths (0 = the rect alone), and a record is clipped to the rect and to each of them. Its rect is then also bounded by the paths' boxes. clip_paths is a path table like path: xy, run_offset, path_offset (one shape per entry) and evenodd.

  • Opacity groups: a group whose only effect is an opacity below 1. record$group is the 1-based row of groups (the innermost such group the record is drawn in, 0 = none). groups has alpha and parent (1-based, 0 = top level). A client draws a group's records into their own layer and composites it at alpha.

Masks, blend modes, blur and shadow effects, hatches, patterns, repeating or reflecting gradients and gradient strokes stay flagged.

  • Flagged runs (VW-30): record$run is the run of flagged marks a record belongs to (1-based, 0 = none) and runs their count. A run is a stretch of flagged marks in paint order that no exactly drawn mark interrupts; every record of a node with a flagged record, and of an opacity group holding one, is in it. scene_png(layer = "keyed_flagged", run = k) draws run k, so a client can draw the exact records itself and composite each run's raster where the run starts.

  • Blend modes in runs (VW-32): run_blend gives, per run, how its raster composites onto what is beneath it: "normal", or a CSS mix-blend-mode keyword ("multiply", "screen", ...) when the run is exactly the marks of one group with that blend mode drawn onto the page, directly or inside groups with no opacity, mask, blend or effect, which isolate nothing (a blend root; a run ends where the blend root changes). Rendered on its own, such a run's raster is its marks unblended, and compositing it with that mode reproduces the blend. A blend nested inside a mask, an effect or an opacity group happens within that group's raster, so its run is "normal". "" would mark a run that cannot be composited from its raster; current lists have none.

What stage 1 does not reproduce

Such marks are still listed, so they can be hit-tested, but flags marks them and a client should fall back to its approximate path for them: 1 a gradient, pattern or hatch paint (the paint's colour is NA); 2 a clip that is not an axis-aligned rectangle (the clip is not listed); 4 a mark inside a group with opacity, blend mode, mask or effect; 8 a text label (the geometry is its box); 16 pick-only: a keyed mark that paints nothing (an invisible hover target such as a fill = NA rect, circle, marker or polygon). Its geometry is listed and its paint has fill and stroke NA, so a client hit-tests it but draws nothing; 32 inside a group with a blend mode (with 4): the mark mixes with what is painted beneath it, so its run's raster reproduces it only when composited with the run's run_blend mode. Images do not appear at all.
